subject: SLO + Burst Capacity: proposed test plan & clarifications
snippet: Recap from today's SLO/scale discussion + proposed joint load test and warm-pool targets.
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: Elena Torres <etorres@medlytics.com>, James Liu <james.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: SLO + Burst Capacity: proposed test plan & clarifications

Hi Elena / James —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. High-level asks you reiterated:

- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for interactive agents; p99 retry target <= 800ms for 1–2s requests.
- Throughput: baseline 300 RPS sustained, burst to 1,200 RPS for 90s windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent streams ~120, peak ~400 (cross-region).
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required — chunk latency target <= 60ms for first-byte and steady chunking every 50–80ms.

On autoscaling/burst behavior we covered: warm-pool approach preferred to avoid cold start tails. Actionable assumptions I captured:
- Warm pool of GPU workers per region (min warm capacity = 2 GPUs; bump plan to 6 GPUs during predictable windows).
- Scale-up to fully provisioned capacity within 45–90s (depends on instance family and image warm-up).
- Request queueing: soft queue depth to preserve SLOs — we propose bounded queue with backpressure and fallbacks to a lower-cost model variant.

Attachments: attached SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (table mapping workload slices -> p50/p95/p99), burst-capacity-proposal.pdf (cost/ops options).

Proposed next steps:
1) Agree on a joint load test: Redwood will run a staged load test (baseline -> progressive ramp -> 90s bursts) against your staging endpoint; we capture p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rates, and streaming chunk timings.
2) Define warm-pool baseline (we suggest starting at 4 GPUs per region for the first week of testing).
3) Run one canary day in staging, then propose production schedule.

Can you confirm that the SLO numbers above match what you expect? If yes, Neha and Ben from our infra team can draft the test harness and run the first test next Thursday (25th) or Friday (26th).

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer

Hi Elena — quick technical follow-up to answer your questions:

1) Warm-pool cost delta (very rough, depends on instance type):
   - 4 x A10G-style nodes warm: ~ $6k–$9k / month (on our reserved pricing).
   - 6 x A10G-style nodes warm: ~ $9k–$13k / month.
   We can provide a line-item once you pick region/instance family.

2) Scale-up breakdown:
   - Orchestration/provisioning (spin up VM/container): ~20–35s typical.
   - Model weight load & KV warming: ~15–40s depending on quantization and model size.
   - Network attach / health checks: ~5–15s.
   So the 45–90s window is additive across those phases; if you pre-warm model weights (warm images) you'll hit ~45–55s more often.

3) Mitigations for degraded streaming chunking during bursts:
   - Activate prefix KV cache for repeated conversational prefixes (reduces token compute).
   - Route a percentage of requests to a lower-cost compatible variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized) while preserving first-byte latency via warmed instances.
   - Short-term token-shedding / rate-limit per-session to preserve interactive experience for a subset of users.

Test harness notes: we'll instrument chunk first-byte latency and per-chunk inter-arrival. We can ship an initial harness (JMeter-based) that emits streaming clients.

Happy to join the call on the 25th to run the instrumentation and interpret results.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com
